title: Database Relationships
summary: One-to-many, many-to-many, eager loading strategies, and solving the N+1 problem.

sections.content:
from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column, relationship

class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    items: Mapped[list["Item"]] = relationship(back_populates="owner", cascade="all, delete-orphan")

class Item(Base):
    __tablename__ = "items"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(200))
    owner_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("users.id"))
    owner: Mapped["User"] = relationship(back_populates="items")
cascade='all, delete-orphan' means deleting a user automatically deletes their items.
In async SQLAlchemy, lazy loading fails (MissingGreenlet error). You MUST explicitly eager-load related data:

from sqlalchemy.orm import selectinload, joinedload

# selectinload: second query for related rows (fast, avoids N+1)
result = await db.execute(
    select(User).options(selectinload(User.items)).where(User.id == user_id)
)
user = result.scalar_one_or_none()

# joinedload: one query with JOIN
result = await db.execute(
    select(User).options(joinedload(User.items)).where(User.id == user_id)
)

rows: Fails in async, causes N+1 in sync

sections.title: N+1 is a performance killer
sections.content: Loading 100 users with lazy loading = 1 query for users + 100 queries for items = 101 queries. Always eager-load what the response needs.

code_challenge.title: One-to-Many with Eager Loading
code_challenge.description: Create User and Item models with a one-to-many relationship. Add GET /users that returns users with their items eagerly loaded.

from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, ForeignKey, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker, DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, relationship, selectinload
from sqlalchemy import String

engine = create_engine("sqlite://", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(bind=engine, autoflush=False, autocommit=False)

class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass

class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)

    items: Mapped[list["Item"]] = relationship(back_populates="owner", cascade="all, delete-orphan")

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(200))
    owner_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("users.id"))
    owner: Mapped["User"] = relationship(back_populates="items")

Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

quiz.question: What is the N+1 problem?
options: 1 query for users + N queries for related data = N+1 total
quiz.explanation: N+1 means 1 query to fetch the parent records, then N queries to fetch related data for each one. It's a major performance killer at scale.

quiz.question: How do you solve N+1 in async SQLAlchemy?
options: Use selectinload or joinedload to eager-load
quiz.explanation: selectinload fetches all related rows in a single additional query. joinedload does it with a JOIN. Both avoid N+1.

quiz.question: What does cascade='all, delete-orphan' do?
options: Deleting the parent deletes its children
quiz.explanation: cascade='all, delete-orphan' ensures that when a parent (User) is deleted, all its children (Items) are also deleted automatically.

quiz.question: Why does lazy loading fail in async SQLAlchemy?
options: MissingGreenlet: async sessions don't support implicit lazy loads
quiz.explanation: Async sessions don't support implicit I/O. Lazy loading triggers a query when you access a relationship, but in async that needs await — which can't happen automatically. You get MissingGreenlet.

quiz.question: How do you define a many-to-many relationship?
options: Use a list on both models
Use an association Table with secondary= parameter
quiz.explanation: Define an association table, then use relationship(secondary=item_tag, back_populates=...) on both models to create the many-to-many link.
